answer.why: As an insider I laugh at it straight away: 'confirmed and substantive' is the exact wording of a real career milestone, when you are confirmed in the service and then made substantive in your appointment, so it signals the makers know the details and are not just copying headlines. 'Minister Salary' sounds like clickbait about the most over-discussed topic in Singapore, and I have already sat through that debate in real life. If the game is half as accurate as the name, I would want to see which way it goes.
answer.expect_minister_salary: A satirical or political-outrage game about the pay debate, probably a quick gag where you chase a big pay package. It would be shallow on how the service actually works, with the benchmark formula treated as a punchline and a cartoon version of ministers and civil servants. I would expect to wince at the details, and it would make me wonder if the whole thing is a meme.
answer.expect_confirmed_substantive: A drier, more knowing sim about real public service life: probation, appraisals, acting appointments versus substantive ones, waiting to be confirmed, the quiet anxiety of the ranking exercise. It would be an insider joke that most outsiders would not understand, so it might be a hard sell in a store, but I would expect it to be accurate and funny to people like me.

answer.held_back_by: Nothing really held me back, since I ended as PM. The one drag was STAND sliding for years because I kept choosing principle over politics. The party's own estimate of me was only Senior Minister of State, so I outran it by being boring and clean.
answer.ending_fair_why: A clean file, a PM at 60 and a stable legacy matches how I played. The declassified card was satisfying because it showed ceilings I never saw. I would have liked a clearer link between STAND sliding and still becoming PM.
answer.chase_next: A run that stays inside the service and tops out as Permanent Secretary. I want to see the career where I never enter politics and how the file reads differently.
answer.play_again_why: I finished a full 38 years and want to digest it first. The Indicators and Polling Day loops felt repetitive late on, so I would want a different path before restarting.

tone_breaks.note: The MR grade labels looked odd to me. Real ministerial salary grades are not shown this way, and the MR3 label at one point did not fit the posting.

tone_breaks.line: The formula pays you twice the entry-grade minister's salary
tone_breaks.note: The PM benchmark is a published formula, but 'twice the entry-grade minister' is a simplification that an insider would wince at.

answer.title_fit_why: The game is really about being confirmed in grade and appraised in careful language, not about the salary. The salary is the punchline at the end, not the experience.
